One product has one drawing for every box a value is entered or chosen in — the box a person types in, the box that shows a chosen option, the box of a number, the box of a color — so that a form reads as one form: the same corners, the same height at a size, the same edge at rest, hovered, focused, invalid, read-only and disabled, the same label floating inside a tinted or an outlined box, the same text, placeholder, caret and selection, the same place and size for a glyph at either end. It decides once whether its links are underlined at rest, and marks the ones that lead to another site.

dev.tanrei.vocabulary.rationale: One product shows things that hold other things, to any depth, as rows that open and close: the folders and files of a project, the tiers, groups and tokens of a design system, the categories of a catalogue, the parts of a document. Some of these trees are only read and opened; in others one row is chosen, or several; some are a few rows in a page of text and some are hundreds of rows in a tool; some rows carry a glyph, a note after their name or a short value at their end, some are unavailable, and some fetch what they hold when they are first opened.

dev.tanrei.vocabulary.rationale: One product points to other pages from its own — an article that cites a source, a help page that sends the reader on, a message that carries an address, a list of further reading — and shows some of those places as more than a phrase: the page's title, a sentence about it, a picture where it has one, and the site it is on, in one block that is pressed as a whole. It draws that block set apart by an edge in running text and by tone where one more line would crowd, and lays it out by the room it is given.

One product sends a person a short code — to sign in, to confirm an address or a telephone number, to approve a payment — and asks for it back. The code arrives in a message as a few characters, often in two groups; a row of cells, one per character, says how long it is and how much of it has been entered. It is one text value, and the cells are how that value is drawn.

The place and its three texts are drawn alike wherever a file is asked for.

One product lets people write to one another, or to the product itself — a conversation, a thread under a piece of work, a request for help — and gives them one place to do it, drawn as one capsule: where the text is written, what is attached to it, the product's own actions for it, and the button that sends. It decides once how that capsule is filled and edged, how round it is, how it shows that it is being written in, that something is wrong with the message and that a dragged file will be taken, how far its parts stand from one another and from its edge, how narrow it may be before its actions move below the text, how the count against a limit is written, and how much its send button stands out.
